drug_class: Antineoplastic (cancer-fighting) agent — combination of estrogen and a nitrogen mustard
purpose: Estramustine is used to treat advanced prostate cancer. It helps slow down or stop the growth of cancer cells in the prostate. Your doctor may prescribe it when other treatments have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: Estramustine is a special medicine that combines two cancer-fighting ingredients in one. It works by interfering with the cancer cells ability to grow and divide, and it also uses hormone-like effects to help control prostate cancer. Think of it as a two-in-one approach that attacks the cancer from different angles.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea are common, especially when you first start taking it. You may also notice breast tenderness or swelling, fluid retention (swelling in legs or ankles), fatigue, and decreased sex drive. Some men experience hot flashes as well.
warnings: This medicine can increase your risk of blood clots, which can be serious. Tell your doctor right away if you have chest pain, shortness of breath, or leg swelling and pain. It can also affect your heart and liver, so regular check-ups are important. Do not take it with dairy products or calcium-rich foods or antacids, as they can block the medicine from working properly. This medication is not for use in women or children.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 14 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into smaller doses taken 3 to 4 times a day by mouth. Your doctor will calculate the right amount for you personally. It is best taken on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals, and NOT with milk or dairy products.
